JPM.rationale: JPM presents a strong fundamental case: Q1 2026 revenue accelerated +10.0% YoY to $49.84B with diluted EPS of $5.94 (+17.2% YoY), operating margins stable at ~41.1%, and ROE at the top of its 12-month range at 16.2%. The franchise is best-in-class — #1 Forbes Global 2000 for four consecutive years, top investment bank by fees for 17 straight years, and a universal-bank model generating cross-segment synergies. Morningstar calls it 'an industry outlier in the best possible way.' Valuation is reasonable but not cheap: P/E of 15.5x sits slightly below the midpoint of its 13.7–17.8x 365-day range, and P/B of 2.51x is near the center of its 2.2–2.8x range. The stock is cheaper on earnings today than in December 2025 (P/E 16.9x then vs 15.5x now) despite meaningfully higher EPS. The near-term catalyst is the Q2 2026 earnings report (imminent, with pre-earnings consensus of ~$5.49–5.52 EPS on ~$48.7B revenue per Zacks/Yahoo Finance) — a beat could re-rate the stock, though the historical pattern of post-earnings declines tempers this. The $50B buyback and 10% dividend increase announced after stress test passage (tier 1 capital ratio 14.3%) provide additional support. Offsetting factors: balance-sheet leverage has increased (equity-to-assets from 8.1% to 7.4%), the yield curve is flattening (10y-2y spread at 0.38%), and the stock sits within 2.3% of its 52-week high, limiting near-term upside from multiple expansion. The score of +0.35 reflects strong fundamentals and trajectory (pillar 1) with fair-to-slightly-below-midpoint valuation (pillar 2), plus a modest bump for the imminent Q2 earnings catalyst (pillar 3), tempered by the stock's proximity to highs and the post-earnings decline pattern.
